{6} That is: {And among the people is he who} is deprived and forsaken, {purchases} (yashtari); that is, he chooses and desires with the eagerness of one who pays a price for a thing, {idle talk} (lahw al-hadith); that is, the discourses that distract the hearts and divert them from the most noble objective. Everything He did and created is to be praised, everything He commanded and forbade is to be praised, and everything He judged among the servants, and between the servants, in this world and the Hereafter, is to be praised.

**{27}** Then He informed about the vastness of His speech and the greatness of His word, with an explanation that reaches every heart to its utmost extent, that the intellects are dazzled by it, the hearts are bewildered by it, and those of understanding and insight wander in seeking to know it. So He said: ﴿And if all the trees on earth were pens﴾, with which to write, ﴿and the sea, with seven more seas to supply its ink﴾, as ink to be drawn upon, ﴿the pens would be worn out, and the ink would be exhausted, but the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾. This is not an exaggeration with no reality. Rather, because Allah, blessed and exalted, knew that minds fall short of encompassing some of His attributes, and knew that knowing Him is the greatest blessing He bestows upon His servants and the most noble virtue they can attain, yet it cannot be grasped in its full manner, He nonetheless taught that what cannot be grasped entirely should not be left entirely. So He alerted them to some of it, an alert by which their hearts are illuminated, their breasts are expanded, and they may draw inferences from what they have reached to what they have not reached. They would say as the best of them and the most knowledgeable of his Lord said: "I cannot count Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself." Otherwise, the matter is far greater and more magnificent than that.

This illustration is a way of bringing a meaning that cannot be attained near to people's understandings and minds. Otherwise, even if the trees were multiplied many times over what was mentioned, and the seas were extended by manifold multiples, their exhaustion and ending could still be imagined, because they are created. But the speech of Allah, exalted, cannot be imagined to be exhausted. Indeed, the legal and rational proofs show us that it has no exhaustion and no end, for everything comes to an end except the Creator and His attributes: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾. When the intellect conceives the reality of His being the First and the Last, and that whatever the mind supposes of past times, however far the supposition and estimation are extended, He is before that without end; and that whatever the mind and intellect suppose of future times, however far the supposition and estimation are extended, and whoever agrees with it in heart and tongue, Allah is after that without limit or end. Allah, at all times, judges, speaks, says, and acts as He wills, and whenever He wills, nothing prevents Him from any of His words or deeds. So when the intellect conceives this, it knows that the example Allah gave for His speech is so that the servants may grasp some of it; otherwise the matter is greater and more magnificent.

Then He mentioned the majesty of His might and the perfection of His wisdom, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾. That is: to Him belongs all might, and whatever strength exists in the upper and lower worlds is only from Him. He is the One who gave it to the creatures, so there is no power nor strength except by Him. By His might He overpowered all creatures, disposed of them and governed them; by His wisdom He created the creation, began it with wisdom, and made its end and purpose wisdom. Likewise, His command and prohibition exist by wisdom, and their intended end is wisdom. He is the Wise in His creation and His command.

**{28}** Then He mentioned the greatness of His power and its perfection, and that the intellect cannot conceive it. So He said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾. This is a matter that bewilders the intellects: that the creation of all creatures, despite their multitude, and their resurrection after their death and dispersal, is in a single instant, like His creating one soul. So there is no basis for deeming the resurrection, the rising up, and the recompense for deeds unlikely, except through ignorance of the greatness of Allah and the strength of His power. Then He mentioned the all-encompassing nature of His hearing of all things heard and His sight of all things seen, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾.

{29} This also includes His sole control and governance, and the vastness of His dominion: He causes the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, i.e., He makes one of them enter upon the other; so when one enters, the other departs. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running with precise arrangement and order that has never failed since He created them, so that through this He establishes for the servants benefits and advantages, in their religion and their worldly life, by which they may take heed and profit. And each of them {runs for a specified term}: when that term comes, their motion ceases and their authority is brought to an end, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection, when the sun is wound up and the moon is eclipsed, the abode of this world comes to an end, and the Hereafter begins. {And indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do}: of good and evil. {Acquainted}: nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for those deeds, with reward for the obedient and punishment for the disobedient.

{30} {That}: the One who has shown you of His greatness and attributes what He has shown, {is because Allah is the Truth}: in His essence and in His attributes; His religion is true, His messengers are true, His promise is true, His threat is true, and His worship is the truth. {And that what they call upon besides Him is the falsehood}: in its essence and attributes; were it not for Allah's bringing it into existence, it would not exist, and were it not for His sustaining it, it would not remain; so if it is false, then worship of it is even more false. {And that Allah is the Most High}: in His essence, above all His creation, whose attributes are too exalted to be compared with the attributes of [any of the creatures], and He is exalted over the creation, subduing them; {the Most Great}: to whom belongs greatness in His essence and attributes, and to whom belongs grandeur in the hearts of the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.

{31} That is: Do you not see, among the signs of His power, His mercy and His care for His servants, that He subjected the sea so that ships run upon it by His decree, His kindness and His beneficence? {That He may show you of His signs}: in them are benefit and lessons. {Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one}: it is they who benefit from the signs. {Patient} in adversity, {grateful} in ease; patient in obedience to God, in refraining from disobedience to Him, and in His decrees; grateful to God for His religious and worldly blessings.

{32} The Exalted mentions the condition of people when they board the sea and the waves cover them like shade above them: they sincerely make their supplication and worship sincerely to God. {Then when He delivers them to the land}, they divide into two groups: a group that is moderate (muqtasid), meaning they did not perform the thanks due to God in its complete form, but rather they are sinners who wrong themselves; and a group that is disbelieving in God's blessing, denying it. Therefore He said: {And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate}; that is, treacherous, and among their treachery is that he covenanted with his Lord, "If You deliver us from the sea and its hardship, we will surely be among the thankful," and then he betrayed, and did not fulfill that. {Ungrateful}: for the blessings of God. So is it fitting for one whom God has delivered from this hardship to do anything other than fully perform the thanks for God's blessings?!

{33} Allah commands mankind to have taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of Allah), which is carrying out His commands and abandoning what He has forbidden, and He reminds them to fear the Day of Resurrection, the terrible Day on which every person will be concerned only with himself. ﴿No father will avail anything for his son, nor will a son avail anything for his father﴾: he will not add to his good deeds or reduce his bad deeds. Each servant's deeds will have been completed, and his recompense will have been determined for him. Reminding oneself of this awesome Day strengthens the servant and makes taqwa of Allah easier for him, and this is from the mercy of Allah toward His servants. He commands them to have taqwa, in which lies their happiness; He promises them reward for it, warns them of punishment, and urges them toward Him through admonitions and warnings. So to You belongs all praise, O Lord of the worlds. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾: so do not doubt it, and do not act like one who does not believe it. For this reason He says: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾: by its adornments, its ornaments, and the trials and tribulations within it. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾: who is Satan, who never ceases to deceive man and is never heedless of him at any time. Allah has a right over His servants, and He has promised them an appointed time at which He will recompense them for their deeds, and whether they fulfilled His right or fell short in it. This is a matter that must be given attention, and the servant should keep it before his eyes and make it the capital of the trade he strives for. Among the greatest obstacles to it and the barriers before it are the seductive world and the whispering, enticing Satan. Thus Allah forbade His servants that the world should deceive them, or that the Deceiver should deceive them about Allah, ﴿He promises them and gives them false hopes, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾.

{34} It is established that God, exalted is He, encompasses knowledge of the Unseen and the seen, the outward and the inward, and God may inform His servants of many unseen matters. These five matters are among those whose knowledge God has withheld from all creation; no prophet sent and no angel brought near knows them, let alone anyone else. So He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾; that is, He knows when it will arrive, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It will not come to you except suddenly..."﴾ [7:187], the verse. ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾; that is, He alone sends it down and knows the time of its descent. ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾: He is the One who brought into being what is in them and knows what it is, whether male or female. Therefore the angel appointed over the wombs asks his Lord: "Is it male or female?" and God decrees what He wills. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾: of the earning of its religion and its worldly life. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾. Rather, God, exalted is He, is the One specially possessed of the knowledge of all of this. Since He specified these things, He generalized His knowledge to all things, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing, Acquainted﴾: encompassing the outward and the inward, the hidden, the concealed, and the secrets. And among His perfect wisdom is that He concealed the knowledge of these five from the servants, because in that there are benefits that are not hidden from one who reflects upon them.

The tafsir of Surah Luqman is completed by the grace and help of Allah, and praise be to Allah.
